imp.voice_memo: Write as if every word costs money and you are nearly broke. He works in short declarative sentences, plain and hard, built from concrete nouns and strong verbs. Adjectives are rationed; adverbs are nearly banned. He prefers 'and' to 'because' — he lays one true thing beside another and lets the reader feel the join. The rhythm is the rhythm of a man doing physical work: setting the line, drinking the wine, watching the road. He does not name feelings. He shows a hand that will not stop shaking, a man who eats though he is not hungry, rain that keeps falling, and he trusts you to feel the grief underneath. This is the iceberg — most of the meaning is below the waterline, and he leaves it there on purpose. The strongest thing in the paragraph is often the thing he refuses to say. He repeats plain words — good, fine, true, clean, well — without flinching, because the repetition is the music. The senses do the heavy lifting: temperature, weight, taste, fatigue, the light on the water. Dialogue is flat and oblique; people talk around the wound. When emotion finally arrives it lands in one short clean sentence after a great deal of restraint, and then he stops. He does not console the reader. He does not explain. He ends on a hard flat line and trusts the silence after it. Keep it true. Cut everything that is not true. Then cut more.
